title: Atomium
blurb: The Atomium in Brussels, built for the 1958 World's Fair: nine 18 m stainless-steel spheres arranged as an iron crystal unit cell magnified 165 billion times, joined by twenty tubes and rising 102 m over the Heysel Plateau.

systems.name: Nine spheres
systems.description: Nine 18 m stainless-steel-clad spheres arranged as an iron crystal unit cell magnified 165 billion times: eight cube vertices plus the body center.

systems.name: Cladding, windows and lighting
systems.description: The stainless-steel cladding panels, window bands and LED meridian lighting of the nine spheres.

systems.name: Edge tubes
systems.description: The twelve 3 m tubes along the cube edges, enclosing stairs and escalators between the spheres.

systems.name: Diagonal tubes
systems.description: The eight tubes from the cube vertices to the central sphere; the two vertical ones carry the lift.

systems.name: Supports and foundations
systems.description: The three support tripods under the lower spheres, added after wind-tunnel tests showed the original design would topple, with the foundation pier and raft.

systems.name: Interior circulation
systems.description: The lift in the central vertical tube, the escalators in the oblique tubes and the stairs in the edge tubes.

systems.name: Top sphere restaurant
systems.description: The panoramic restaurant inside the top sphere, with room for about 140 guests.

systems.name: Entrance pavilion
systems.description: The reception pavilion with its boomerang-shaped roof, built during the 2004 to 2006 renovation, and the redeveloped esplanade.

explanations.top sphere: The top sphere, 18 m in diameter, sits 102 m above the ground. It holds the panoramic restaurant, with room for about 140 guests, and the observation deck with views over Brussels. Sphere positions on the cube frame are schematic.
explanations.center sphere: The central sphere of the nine, 18 m in diameter. With its neighbor it holds flexible space that can be rented for events such as film screenings, concerts, parties and conferences. Sphere positions on the cube frame are schematic.
explanations.bottom sphere: The bottom sphere, 18 m in diameter, is reserved for the permanent exhibition on the 1950s, Expo 58 and the construction of the Atomium. Sphere positions on the cube frame are schematic.
explanations.upper sphere 1: One of the three upper outer spheres, 18 m in diameter. The upper outer spheres lack vertical support and are not open to the public, for safety reasons. Sphere positions on the cube frame are schematic.
explanations.lower sphere 1: One of the three lower outer spheres, 18 m in diameter, each carried on a support tripod added after wind-tunnel tests. The lower outer spheres are among the six spheres open to the public, with exhibit halls and public spaces. Sphere positions on the cube frame are schematic.
